newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman says exports rise 23.8 percent in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Oman says exports rise 23.8 percent in Q1 1997.

text.p: Oman's exports rose 23.8 percent to 768.4 million rials ($2.04 billion) in the first quarter of 1997, up from 620.7 million in the year-ago period, statistics from the ministry of development published on Saturday showed.
The value of oil exports was put at 611.5 million rials compared with 480.2 million in the first quarter of 1996, an increase of 27.3 percent, the figures published by the Oman Daily Observer said.
Non-oil exports were worth 48.9 million rials against 46 million in the first quarter of 1996, a rise of 6.3 percent.
Re-exports in the first quarter amounted to 108 million rials, up from 94.5 million the previous year.
Oman is a major non-OPEC oil producer. It produces 900,000 barrels per day of oil, which accounts for nearly three-quarters of government revenues. ($1=0.377 rials)
